task: Reconcile VERIFIED parent proof metadata with persisted execution identity while retaining fail-closed detection of all other post-verification changes.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: A CLOSED parent proof projection has its own verified implementation main, followed by a separate metadata commit. The generic CLOSED plan Truth Gate wrongly marks its deterministic proof artifact as post-verification material drift, preventing exact-head parent closure even when all three child receipts and canonical source identities match.
observableOutcomes: A trusted CLOSED parent projection with an independently recomputed proof artifact, exact persisted state and metadata-only commit receives PASS at its actual PR head.
An invalid proof artifact, wrong immutable source commit, wrong final implementation main, forged child receipts or mismatched canonical persistence always receives BLOCK.
Any source code, fixture or unrelated metadata change after the verified implementation commit continues to receive DEV_LIFECYCLE_POST_VERIFICATION_MATERIAL_CHANGE.
A generic CLOSED plan or one with an unrecognized parent context never receives a broad metadata exemption.
Exact-head completion proof remains tied to the canonical persisted state and is independently checked before parent closure proceeds.
unresolvedRisks: The remote canonical parent state may advance during verification, so exact state and head identities must be inspected and mismatches fail closed.
A forged plan and proof artifact can share self-consistent data, requiring independent source, receipt, main-advance and persistence verification.
The repair must remain strictly confined to Control Plane truth classification and regression tests, with no modification to the executor's source receipts.

in: Recognize only the canonical parent-closure proof artifact when its bytes and metadata commit are independently verified.
Read immutable parent source plan and persisted child receipts, and reconstruct the trusted main-advance and proof identities.
Add positive and negative Truth/Lifecycle regression tests for valid and falsified closure metadata.
out: No source branch or execution receipt mutation and no rewrite of persisted canonical release state.
No generic exemption for knowledge JSON, code edits, fixture edits, or future proof changes.
No changes to Storefront, Builder, templates, CI permissions or deployment behavior.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The repair crosses the boundary between verified implementation content and a metadata-only closure commit. It must re-establish immutable source SHA, exact child receipts, trusted main advancement and exact committed artifact bytes before relaxing one specific false positive. Comprehensive adversarial and negative tests protect every other post-verification change.

acceptanceCriteria: The plan-only commit passes Plan Before Code before any implementation file is modified.
A canonical three-child CLOSED state and matching immutable source produce a valid exact-head metadata proof that is not classified as material drift.
A proof with tampered bytes or mismatched context, final main, persisted state or child receipts is blocked deterministically.
Every other changed file after implementation verification remains material drift and blocks closure.
The exact-head CI and canonical executor authority decide final closure; no manual state edits or gate exemptions.
invariants: The immutable source commit and every CLOSED child receipt are read-only inputs.
Only an independently verified parent artifact at the exact committed metadata head is exempt from generic material-change classification.
A valid proof requires source plan, parent execution, final main, metadata ancestry and bytes to agree.
All other post-verification material changes remain blocked, including any unrelated knowledge file.
No code path may promote parent closure without exact-head verification and canonical state persistence.
forbiddenStates: Forged parent proof accepted as verification authority
Source SHA or final main SHA mismatch accepted
Mismatched or missing U01-U03 child receipt accepted
Generic CLOSED plan material drift silently accepted
Unverified implementation change falsely classified as metadata

failureModes: The proof is accepted solely because its path matches a planned file pattern.
The artifact and plan are both forged to appear self-consistent without authoritative child receipts.
A different source SHA or final main is substituted after verification.
The metadata commit contains other material files or has an untrusted parent.
The canonical state remains stale relative to the PR head after a repair commit.
edgeCases: Canonical proof is valid and is the sole non-plan change.
Artifact is tampered by one byte or missing entirely.
Canonical context has wrong source, parent ID, main SHA or receipt digest.
Remote state includes an unclosed child or stale persistence head.
A second JSON file or TypeScript file changed after verified head.
Metadata commit has two parents or wrong single parent.
Generic CLOSED task declares a proof-looking filename without canonical context.
Source plan digest differs despite a matching reported task identifier.

alternatives.summary: Recompute the exact canonical parent proof through existing source and state authority before classifying its committed artifact.
alternatives.reason: Only independently reconstructed receipts, source identity, final main and committed bytes can justify a narrowly scoped metadata exception.

alternatives.summary: Ignore all files within the parent closure proof directory during completed-plan evaluation.
alternatives.reason: A pathname exemption would allow forged or unrelated post-verification changes to evade the material drift guard.

alternatives.summary: Rewrite the verified implementation head to the metadata commit and recompute implementation evidence.
alternatives.reason: This destroys the distinction between trusted implementation identity and subsequent closure metadata, creating a circular truth claim.

specialistReviews.finding: Generic lifecycle evaluation conflates trusted closure metadata with implementation drift.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require an explicit independently validated exact-head parent proof classification.

specialistReviews.finding: Self-consistent proof fields alone can be forged and cannot authorize exceptions.
specialistReviews.resolution: Rebuild expected proof from immutable source and persisted receipts, and compare exact committed bytes.

specialistReviews.finding: Source, child receipts, trusted main advance and canonical state are separate identity authorities.
specialistReviews.resolution: Fail closed on any mismatch, including stale persisted projection or wrong metadata commit parent.

specialistReviews.finding: A repaired PR head can diverge from persisted canonical closure head.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep exact persistence binding and require executor reconciliation before merge.

specialistReviews.finding: A generic knowledge path whitelist would create material drift bypasses.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve negative regressions for arbitrary file edits, forged contexts and false proof prefixes.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Forged proof bytes; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A file path match could hide different committed bytes.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Derive expected artifact bytes and compare to exact git object.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Forged source plan; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A mutable plan can impersonate the parent source identity.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Read the source plan from immutable source commit and validate plan projection.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Wrong final main; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A metadata commit can target a different implementation parent.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Check exact one-parent ancestry and trusted main-advance reconstruction.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Unclosed child receipt; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A synthetic parent state can claim complete implementation.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Read persisted state and require every child CLOSED with valid closeReceipt.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Receipt digest mismatch; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A copied proof could reuse old child receipt signatures.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Rebuild context and compare all ordered child close-receipt digests.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Stale persistence; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A repaired PR head may not match canonical closure persistence.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Block stale parent projection until canonical executor reconciles it.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Extra post verification file; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: An unrelated material change might accompany correct proof metadata.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Permit exactly the verified artifact while rejecting every other changed file.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: Generic closed plan; validate exact closure transition constraints.
challenge.finding: Risk: A normal CLOSED task may have proof-looking JSON beside its plan.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Without canonical parent context and independent evidence, preserve normal material classification.

proofPlan: Commit a complete plan-only revision and obtain Plan Before Code proof before touching implementation code.
Add independent source state and artifact verification to CLOSED parent Truth Gate evaluation.
Unit test valid parent metadata allowance and forged, stale, extra-change and generic CLOSED denial cases.
Run full scoped tests and negative fault scenarios before using the exact PR-head CI.
Require the canonical executor to reconcile repaired parent closure persistence and deliver final exact-head proof.
Only after every gate passes permit the canonical CLOSED receipt; avoid manual state edits.

requirements.requirement: Only a fully reconstructed and exact-head-committed parent proof shall be treated as lifecycle metadata after verification.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Forged parent artifact and wrong receipt source identities remain blocked.
Unrelated material modifications after verification are still blocked.
Generic CLOSED plans retain the original material change guard.
